summary.oneLiner: Niche, cash-generative SS flexible-flow maker pivoting up the value chain — value-added products (assemblies/fittings/bellows/skids) now 54% of 9M sales — with a new, high-optionality leg in data-center liquid-cooling skid assemblies under a 5-year India-exclusive deal with a US multinational. Highest-ever quarterly revenue/EBITDA/PAT despite a 50% US tariff and an 8% price discount, offset by internal cost engineering and supply-chain sharing.
summary.business: Aeroflex Industries manufactures stainless-steel corrugated flexible hoses (with and without braiding), metal bellows and engineered assemblies/fittings used for fluid transfer and flow control across oil & gas, petrochemicals, power generation, fire suppression, ports and terminal handling, chemicals, food and pharmaceutical processing, and solar energy. During FY26 it commercialised SFN liquid-cooling skid assemblies, a plug-and-play closed-loop coolant distribution product for high-density AI/data-centre compute hardware, marking its entry into thermal management for digital infrastructure. Its wholly owned subsidiary Hyd-Air Engineering (Chakan, Pune) makes hydraulic fittings and fluid connectors, serving railways, shipbuilding, defence, steel and heavy machinery.

SS flexible hoses: Stainless steel corrugated flexible hoses, with and without braiding
Assemblies and others: Hyd-Air hydraulic fittings and fluid connectors, valves
SFN Skid Assemblies: SFN liquid-cooling skid assemblies for data centres and AI infrastructure

currentContext.strengths: Global technology partnership with a US-based data-centre infrastructure leader providing early entry and commercial traction in liquid cooling|Established global customer relationships and export presence across 90+ countries diversified across Americas, Europe and Asia|Deep innovation pipeline: 58 products under R&D across various stages, including 16 specifically for data-centre liquid cooling|Engineering differentiation, product quality and customer intimacy cited as basis for competing against new entrants|Investment in automation and robotic welding lines strengthening throughput and product quality|Vertical integration and end-to-end fluid-flow capability via Hyd-Air Engineering acquisition, with German technology-enabled capabilities
currentContext.strategies: Expand the liquid-cooling solutions business for data centres and AI infrastructure as a new growth vertical, building on the partnership with a US-based data-centre infrastructure technology leader|Move up the value chain by increasing the contribution of assemblies and metal bellows relative to standard hose products|Strengthen automation and advanced manufacturing capabilities (robotic welding lines, automatic welding station, annealing plant, Industry 4.0 / SAP ERP adoption)|Deepen vertical integration and end-to-end fluid-flow solutions capability through the Hyd-Air Engineering acquisition|Pursue strategic expansion of international presence, including initiatives in the United States and the Middle East|Diversify into adjacent growth vectors: hydrogen infrastructure, EV thermal management, HVAC, semiconductors, robotics and automation|Continue evaluating selective opportunities to enhance capabilities and broaden market reach|Manage thermal-management adoption risk through phased capacity expansion, active customer engagement and a diversified domestic/international go-to-market approach|Dividend payments are governed by the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy, framed in accordance with Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations (policy available on the Company's website); the final dividend for FY26 is being recommended for member approval under that policy. Governance policy framework additionally includes Risk Management, Succession, ESOP, Related Party Transaction, Policy on Material Subsidiaries, and Policy for Identification of Material Litigations/Group Companies/Outstanding Dues, indicating a structured, board-governed approach to capital and risk stewardship rather than a stated payout ratio.
currentContext.expansion: Aeroflex pursued capacity expansion on multiple fronts during FY26 and into FY27. SS flexible hose capacity was augmented by 1.0 million metres in Q3FY26 to 17.5 million metres p.a. installed as at 31 March 2026 (~70% utilisation during the year), with a further expansion to 20 million metres p.a. on track for completion by Q2FY27. In the assemblies business, two robotic welding lines were added in Q4FY26 (46 assembly stations as at 31 March 2026), and the Company plans to add more assembly stations together with commissioning an automatic welding station and annealing plant by December 2026. The new SFN liquid-cooling skid assembly line was scaled from 2,000 units p.a. installed capacity in December 2025 to 6,000 units p.a. as at 31 March 2026, with further expansion to 9,000 units targeted in Q2FY27 en route to a total installed capacity of 15,000 units p.a. by Q2FY27. Hyd-Air Engineering (wholly owned subsidiary) upgraded its quality laboratory and R&D centre at Chakan, Pune. The Company also derives benefits from a 750 KW rooftop solar power project installed at its Taloja manufacturing facility (installed in the previous financial year) and operates a NABL-accredited Research & Development Laboratory; during FY26 it incurred R&D expenditure of ₹395.50 lakhs focused on new product development, including liquid-cooling solutions for data centres and AI infrastructure.
currentContext.mdna: India's sustained industrial capex cycle (National Infrastructure Pipeline, PM Gati Shakti, PLI schemes) is expanding addressable demand across oil & gas, petrochemicals, refineries, power generation, ports and terminals, and firefighting systems|Make in India initiative and defence indigenisation (IDDM framework) are opening new addressable markets in aerospace and defence for certified Indian manufacturers|Structural shift toward liquid cooling in data-centre and AI infrastructure is the most significant medium/long-term opportunity; global liquid-cooling market expected to grow nearly tenfold by 2034 and India's nearly fourteen-fold over the same period|Energy transition and clean-energy infrastructure (green hydrogen, solar) expanding application of flow-control products in high-purity gas handling and thermal management|India's emerging semiconductor fabrication and electronics manufacturing base creating demand for ultra-precision vacuum/wafer-handling products|Rapid EV adoption creating demand for bellows in battery thermal management and cooling|Diversified end-market presence and strong customer stickiness helping sustain growth momentum despite headwinds in certain export markets|Domestic market witnessed particularly strong growth driven by project demand across ports, irrigation, oil & gas, petrochemicals and steel sectors|Increasing adoption of value-added products (assemblies, bellows, liquid-cooling solutions) expected to further strengthen business mix and enhance profitability|Pace of liquid-cooling adoption in Indian data centres (early-stage relative to North America/Europe) flagged as principal risk moderating near-term revenue ramp for the thermal-management business|Competitive intensity in both core and new businesses is a continuous risk addressed through engineering differentiation, product quality and customer intimacy|Aeroflex enters FY27 with a strong outlook, supported by a healthy order pipeline, established customer relationships and a strong balance sheet|Continuous orders and dispatches under the long-term agreement with the US-based data-centre infrastructure partner reflect the strength of the Company's engineering capabilities and R&D expertise

risks.note: Geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions, tariff measures, sanctions and regional economic disruptions may affect demand, pricing and supply-chain continuity across the Company's 90+ export markets; the ongoing Middle East conflict and residual trade-policy uncertainty add to global fragmentation risk.
Currency fluctuations may affect export realisations, profitability and the value of foreign-currency-denominated transactions, given the Company's significant international revenue exposure.

In the thermal-management business, the pace of liquid-cooling adoption in Indian data centres remains at an early stage relative to North America and Europe; longer customer qualification cycles, higher initial investment costs for operators and the prevalence of gas-based cooling in India's installed base may moderate the near-term revenue ramp.

Slowdowns in industrial activity, changes in customer spending patterns, competitive intensity and sector-specific demand fluctuations may impact order inflows, capacity utilisation and revenue growth.
Disruptions in raw material availability, logistics bottlenecks or supplier concentration may affect production schedules and customer deliveries.

Changes in environmental regulations, export controls, trade policies, taxation frameworks and industry-specific standards across domestic and international markets may increase compliance costs or affect market access.
Manufacturing interruptions arising from equipment failures, process inefficiencies, utility disruptions or human error may impact productivity, quality and customer commitments.
Increasing reliance on digital systems exposes the Company to risks related to cyberattacks, data breaches and system failures.

thesis: Niche, cash-generative SS flexible-flow maker pivoting up the value chain — value-added products (assemblies/fittings/bellows/skids) now 54% of 9M sales — with a new, high-optionality leg in data-center liquid-cooling skid assemblies under a 5-year India-exclusive deal with a US multinational. Highest-ever quarterly revenue/EBITDA/PAT despite a 50% US tariff and an 8% price discount, offset by internal cost engineering and supply-chain sharing.
guidance: EBITDA margin target 23–25% over next couple of years (vs ~20–21% two years ago); aspiration to ~25%.
If 50% US tariff is resolved, margins materially higher (mgmt would not quantify; an analyst floated +400–500bps).
Hose+assembly capacity reaches 20M meters; balance 2.5M meters phased to Q2FY27. Peak hose+assembly revenue INR 650–675 cr (assuming ~70% from assemblies).
Liquid-cooling peak revenue INR 300–350 cr, peak utilization ~FY29 (2–2.5 yrs); near-term dispatch pipeline INR 45 cr.
Metal bellows: current run-rate INR 12 cr → INR 36 cr in next few quarters; peak ~INR 85 cr by end-FY28/start-FY29 (behind schedule due to US tariff delays).
Hyd-Air: INR 45 cr peak at current capacity (capex to expand coming soon).
Aggregate peak revenue potential >INR 1,000 cr over next ~3 years.
order book: Liquid-cooling skid pipeline INR 45 cr scheduled for dispatch per partner's plan (India-only currently).
US: no order cancellations; repeat orders from existing customers resuming; new-customer/OEM onboarding delayed by tariffs.
Domestic order traction in steel, ports & terminals, chemicals; Hyd-Air strong in railways.
segment: Hoses & assemblies — core; assemblies (hose+braid) the growth focus, mgmt wants share to keep rising. Capacity +1M meters added this month → 17.5M; → 20M phased by Q2FY27.
Metal bellows — run-rate INR 12 cr; Phase-2 (120k→300k units) deferred until Phase-1 optimal.
Miniature metal bellows — capex cut INR 23 cr → INR 10.5 cr; capacity 240k → ~50–60k units/yr; peak only ~INR 8–9 cr; demand slower than hoped.

Liquid cooling (skid assemblies) — first commercial dispatch done; capacity 2,000 → 15,000 units/yr by Jun-2026; new Chakan (Pune) support plant; capex <INR 100 cr; ~INR 3 lakh/piece realization at 80% utilization. Margins better than hoses, in line with assemblies.
Hyd-Air (subsidiary) — revenue INR 8.5 cr (vs INR 2.9 cr YoY); ~70% utilization; capex planned.
growth: Quarterly exports +30% YoY (EU major contributor) despite tariffs; 9M export growth still single-digit due to very weak Q1.
EU framed as next strong leg — India–EU FTA expected to boost competitiveness vs Turkey (duty-free EU access); EU was flat ~3 years.
Domestic up strongly 9M — new ports/terminals & chemical customers, deeper wallet share in steel.
Liquid-cooling TAM: global ~$3bn now, ~33% CAGR → ~$21bn over 6–7 yrs.
margins: Q3 EBITDA margin 23.5–23.6%, mix-led (value-added 54%). Took 8% price discount on US tariff but protected bottom line via internal cost optimization + vendor cost-sharing.
Liquid-cooling margins undisclosed (single-customer confidentiality) but > hoses, ~= assemblies.
RM (SS wire/coil) managed via back-to-back planning + long-term supplier contracts; prices broadly stable last couple of years.
capex: 9M FY26 capex ~INR 36 cr (liquid cooling ~INR 9 cr; bellows ~INR 5 cr; hoses/assemblies/welding ~INR 22 cr).
Planned go-forward capex (incl. working capital) ~INR 97 cr — hoses balance, skid-assembly expansion (15k units by Jun-26), annealing plant + robotic/automated welding (complete by end-CY2026).
Miniature bellows capex rationalized to reduce gestation risk / speed payback; funds redeployed to higher-visibility projects.
capital allocation: No debt; does not plan to raise debt. Preferential allotment in-principle approval received; funds expected imminently.
Disciplined: cut low-visibility miniature-bellows outlay, redeploy to demand-backed projects (liquid cooling, hoses, annealing).
risks: US tariff (50%) — biggest market (US ~55% of exports); blocks new-customer onboarding; bellows ramp delayed.
Heavy export concentration (74% sales; EU+US ~85% of exports) and single-customer dependence in liquid cooling (5-yr exclusive, India-only).
Liquid-cooling demand entirely partner-forecast-driven; data-center capex cyclicality.
Execution: capacity additions across hoses/assemblies/bellows running behind schedule.
mgmt tone: Confident but measured ("Q3 good, not very good"); candid on Q1 weakness, bellows being behind schedule, and tariff drag on new customers. Emphasis on long-term margin path and moat narrative.
non-obvious: Liquid-cooling skid is flow-control IP adaptable beyond data centers (large machinery, semiconductor, HVAC, EV cooling) — collapse-of-DC optionality.
Partner intends to make the India entity a global supply hub for skid assemblies in 3–4 years (exports possible ~6 months out) — large latent upside beyond the India-only INR 350 cr peak.
Moat = 15–20 yrs flow-control engineering + proprietary flow-simulation software + customer access, not just "changing a hose design."
Assembly growth is self-reinforcing: more assemblies → more captive hose-braid production.
India–EU FTA structurally neutralizes Turkish duty-free advantage in EU.
qoq change log: New: First commercial dispatch of liquid-cooling flow-control components & skid assemblies; skid capacity expansion to 15,000 units (by Jun-26); new Chakan (Pune) support plant.
New: India–EU FTA announced — flagged as near-term EU growth booster.
Cut: Miniature metal bellows capex INR 23 cr → INR 10.5 cr; capacity 240k → ~50–60k units/yr (vs prior 240k plan); metal-bellows Phase-2 (120k→300k) deferred.
Disclosure gap vs prior quarters: end-user industry mix not provided this quarter (analyst flagged); skid margins withheld (single-customer confidentiality).
Capacity: +1M meters hose added this month → 17.5M; balance 2.5M phased to Q2FY27.
Subsidiary: Hyd-Air revenue jumped to INR 8.5 cr (from INR 2.9 cr YoY); capex expansion to be announced.
Mix: Value-added products now 54% of 9M sales (vs ~52% assemblies traction noted by analyst).

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
themes.driver: DC cooling LOIs converting (VENUSPIPES, AEROFLEX); hyperscaler/colo India capex (CUMMINSIND gensets, BLUESTARCO MEP); STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler optical-connectivity deal and 2.4x QoQ order-book jump to INR18,618cr; GPU/AI-infra orders.
